newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Tuesday:

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida announced three news conferences on Wednesday's Commission weekly meeting starting with Commissioner Joao de Deus Pinheiro on the green paper on future relations with ACP coutries at 1200/1100 GMT followed by Commissioner Anita Gradin on the communication on trafficking in women for sexual purposes at 1230/1130 GMT and Commissioner Edith Cresson on research and development at 1300/1200 GMT.
Vale de Almeida said the Commission briefing would therefore be brought forward from 1200/1100 GMT to 1145/1045 GMT.

Spokeswoman Sarah Lambert said the Commission was pleased that the railwaymen's demonstration would take place in Brussels. She said the Commission understood the unions' concerns and recognize the need for changes in the railway sector and for consultations between the various partners. Lambert also announced a Commission white paper on this issue.

Spokeswoman Sophie Petzell said the Commission, jointly with the European Parliament and the Presidency of the European Union, were organizing a seminar on prevention of urban criminality linked with drug addiction on Thursday and Friday in the Borschette Centre, followed by a news conference.

Vale de Almeida said Noel Dorr, who presides the committee of ministers' representatives, would hold a news conference on the inter-governmental conference in the Council press room at 1230/1130 GMT on Wednesday.

In answer to a question Constantin Verros said that a fuel assembly containing about 116kg of low enriched non-irradiated uranium had been found on November 14 by EURATOM and International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors. Verros said there was no question of security problems.

In answer to a question, Nikolaus van der Pas said genetically modified maize was not accepted on the European market. He also said he did not know if specific measures had been taken against imports of mixtures of natural and genetically modified maize.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/1033: World Bank/Commission partnership producing results.
- IP/96/1034: Revised list of EU deregulation proposals to Japan.
- IP/96/1035: Anti-dumping measures on unbleached cotton fabric.
- IP/96/1036: Commission presents strategy paper for reducing methane emissions.
- IP/96/1038: Commission sends reasoned opinion to Greece and Portugal for non-implementation of radiation protection directive.
- IP/96/1039: Missing fuel assembly with low enriched uranium found and sealed by EURATOM.
- Eurostat news release No 75/96: Millions of EU tourists cross Mediterranean.
